Before / after

Archivo has no reverse slant. Venture Beyond's Upright and Italic are Archivo's outlines, unchanged. The CSS-skew card shows what Retalic replaces: it looks the same, but it's a transform, not a font. It doesn't work in Figma, and it breaks selection, carets and layout boxes.

Upright · Italic · Retalic

All three variable fonts at any point in the design space. Every line is editable. Retalic has the same character set and spacing as Upright.

Weights

All nine named weights of the selected style and width, taken from the variable fonts.

Outline overlays

Drawn from instances of the variable fonts. Dashed box = advance width, the same in all three styles. Red dashed line = shear pivot (y = 263, half the x-height), the same pivot Omnibus used for Archivo Italic. Retalic is an exact geometric shear of Upright at every location. Italic is a drawn design (see a, e, g, o, s).

Kerning & spacing

Advance widths and kerning are the same as Upright everywhere in the design space. The shear keeps horizontal gaps at every height, so pairs that don't collide in Upright can't collide in Retalic.

Known limitations

  • Retalic is a geometric oblique, not a drawn reverse italic. Round letters (o, e, s, C, O) show the usual oblique stress. Correcting that optically would mean redrawing glyphs, which is out of scope.
  • The fonts are unhinted, like Archivo's variable fonts. This matters only at small sizes on Windows.
  • usWinAscent/Descent are 1107/440, so Ǻ and comma-below accents don't clip on Windows. Archivo's own values clip them at Black Expanded. Line spacing is unchanged.
